prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

A quick charging system for electrically driven vehicles and method for forming an electrically conductive connection between a vehicle and a stationary charging station having a contact device, a charging contact device, and a positioning device. The charging contact device can be electrically contacted in a contact position together with the contact device. The contact device can be positioned in the vertical and horizontal direction relative to the charging contact device and moved to the contact position. The contact device has a contact element carrier with contact elements that can each be electrically contacted together with charge contact elements of the charge contact device, forming contact pairs, in the contact position. A guide device is provided, such that, when the contact device and the charge contact device are brought together, a physical contacting of the contact elements together with the charge contact device is inhibited before reaching the contact position.

outputs.L1: A quick-charging system for electrically driven vehicles, and a method for establishing an electrically conductive connection between a vehicle and a stationary charging station, comprise a contact device, a charging contact device, and a positioning device. The contact device and the charging contact device can be brought into electrical contact in a contact position. The contact device can be positioned vertically and horizontally relative to the charging contact device and moved into the contact position. The contact device includes a contact-element carrier having contact elements, each of which can be brought into electrical contact with a corresponding charging contact element of the charging contact device to form a contact pair in the contact position. A guide device is provided to prevent physical contact between the contact elements and the charging contact device as the contact device and the charging contact device are brought together, until the contact position is reached.
outputs.L2: A rapid-charging system for electric vehicles, and a method for establishing an electrically conductive link between a vehicle and a fixed charging station, include a contact assembly, a charging-contact assembly, and a positioning mechanism. The positioning mechanism moves the contact assembly vertically and horizontally relative to the charging-contact assembly until a contact position is reached, where the two assemblies can be electrically connected. The contact assembly includes a carrier supporting multiple contact elements. In the contact position, each contact element electrically engages a corresponding charging contact element of the charging-contact assembly, thereby creating respective contact pairs. A guide mechanism prevents the contact elements from physically touching the charging-contact assembly as the two assemblies approach one another, until they have reached the contact position.
outputs.L3:
The system enables the rapid charging of electrically driven vehicles through a conductive connection to a stationary charging station. It comprises a contact device, a corresponding charging contact device, and a positioning device that aligns the two components.

The positioning device allows the contact device to move both vertically and horizontally relative to the charging contact device until it reaches the intended contact position. The contact device includes multiple contact elements arranged on a carrier. Once properly aligned, these elements engage with corresponding charging contact elements, forming electrical contact pairs through which charging current can be transmitted.

A guide device ensures that the contact elements remain physically separated from the charging contact elements during the alignment process. This prevents premature or incorrect contact and allows the elements to engage only after the contact device has reached the correct position, thereby supporting a safe and reliable charging connection.
outputs.L4:
A quick-charging system for an electric vehicle includes a stationary charging station and a movable contact device that establishes an electrical connection between the station and the vehicle. To begin charging, the contact device is moved in both the vertical and horizontal directions until its contact elements are properly aligned with corresponding charging contacts on the vehicle or charging station. This multi-axis positioning compensates for variations in vehicle location, height, and alignment, allowing the system to accommodate imperfect parking and differences between vehicle configurations.

The system also includes a guide device that controls the approach of the contact elements. During positioning, the guide device keeps the opposing electrical contacts physically separated, preventing them from touching before they are correctly aligned. Once the contact device reaches the intended contact position, the guide device permits the contact elements to engage the charging contacts in a controlled manner.

By separating the alignment process from the final contact movement, the system reduces the risk of impacts, scraping, arcing, and damage to the electrical interfaces. It also helps prevent incomplete or unstable connections that could interrupt charging or create unsafe operating conditions. After proper engagement has been confirmed, electrical energy can be transferred at a high charging rate. When charging is complete, the contact device is disengaged and returned to a safe position.

This arrangement provides a robust and reliable connection for rapid vehicle charging while reducing mechanical wear and improving operational safety. It is particularly suitable for automated charging installations in which vehicles must be connected quickly and repeatedly with little or no manual intervention.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a quick-charging system that connects an electric vehicle to a stationary charging station using vertically and horizontally positionable contact elements and a guide device that prevents premature physical contact.
counterfactuals.output: A quick-charging system for electrically connecting an electric vehicle to a stationary charging station includes a vehicle-side contact arrangement and a station-side contact arrangement having complementary electrical contact elements. At least one contact arrangement is movable in a vertical direction and a horizontal direction to compensate for variations in vehicle position and height. A guide device engages before the electrical contact elements and aligns the respective contact arrangements during relative movement. The guide device maintains physical separation between the electrical contact elements until a predetermined alignment condition is reached, thereby preventing premature contact, mechanical damage, and electrical arcing. Upon proper alignment, an actuator advances the contact elements into conductive engagement to transfer charging current. The system may further include position sensors, contact-force monitoring, and a controller configured to coordinate alignment, engagement, charging, and disengagement operations.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize an invention for automatically forming an electrically conductive connection between an EV and a fixed charging station.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention provides an automated system for creating a direct electrical connection between an electric vehicle and a stationary charging station. When the vehicle is positioned near the station, sensors identify the location of a vehicle-mounted charging interface. A motorized coupling mechanism then moves one or more conductive contacts into alignment and physically engages them with corresponding contacts on the vehicle.

The system verifies correct positioning and secure contact before energizing the connection. Safety features can include electrical insulation, contact-force monitoring, locking mechanisms, foreign-object detection, and automatic shutoff if misalignment or a fault is detected. After charging, power is disconnected first, and the coupling retracts automatically, allowing the vehicle to depart without manual cable handling.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a concise patent claim overview describing a vehicle charging contact device, a positioning mechanism, paired electrical contacts, and a guide that inhibits contact until the components reach the correct position.
counterfactuals.output:
**Patent Claim Overview:**  
A vehicle charging system comprising: a charging contact device mounted to a vehicle or charging station; a positioning mechanism configured to move the charging contact device into a predetermined charging position; paired electrical contacts carried respectively by the charging contact device and a complementary connector; and a guide configured to align the paired electrical contacts and inhibit their electrical engagement until the charging contact device reaches the predetermined charging position.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe a conductive quick-charging interface for electrically powered vehicles in formal technical language, including its contact carrier, charging contacts, horizontal and vertical alignment, and anti-collision guide mechanism.
counterfactuals.output:
A conductive quick-charging interface for an electrically powered vehicle comprises a vehicle-side contact carrier and a corresponding stationary charging coupler. The contact carrier supports a plurality of electrically insulated charging contacts, including at least positive and negative power contacts and, where required, protective-ground, control, and communication contacts. The charging contacts are configured to establish a low-resistance galvanic connection when the contact carrier and charging coupler are brought into an operative charging position.

The interface includes a horizontal alignment arrangement that permits lateral and/or longitudinal displacement of the contact carrier relative to the vehicle or charging coupler. The horizontal alignment arrangement compensates for vehicle-positioning tolerances and centers the mating contact assemblies before electrical engagement. A vertical alignment arrangement provides height adjustment or compliant vertical movement to compensate for variations in vehicle suspension, road surface, loading condition, and installation height. The horizontal and vertical alignment arrangements may incorporate guides, slides, articulated linkages, resilient mountings, or controlled actuators.

An anti-collision guide mechanism is positioned ahead of, or around, the charging contacts in the direction of engagement. The guide mechanism includes inclined, tapered, curved, or funnel-shaped guide surfaces that contact a complementary structure before the charging contacts can collide. Upon positional deviation, these surfaces generate corrective lateral and/or vertical movement, thereby directing the contact carrier into alignment. Mechanical stops and compliant or breakaway elements may be provided to limit engagement forces and prevent damage in the event of excessive misalignment or an obstruction.

During operation, the anti-collision guide mechanism first performs coarse mechanical alignment, the horizontal and vertical alignment arrangements provide fine positional compensation, and the charging contacts subsequently engage under a controlled contact force. Electrical power transfer is enabled only after correct mechanical engagement and electrical continuity have been verified.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a patent abstract for an automated electric-vehicle charging connector in which station-side and vehicle-side contacts are aligned before electrical engagement, preventing premature contact during coupling.
counterfactuals.output: An automated charging connector for electrically coupling a charging station to an electric vehicle includes a station-side coupling assembly having first electrical contacts and a vehicle-side receptacle having second electrical contacts. One or more alignment features guide the coupling assembly into a predetermined position relative to the receptacle before electrical engagement. At least one set of electrical contacts is movable between a retracted, electrically disengaged position and an extended, electrically engaged position. A mechanical and/or electronic interlock inhibits movement of the contacts toward the engaged position until sensors or cooperating coupling features confirm proper positional and angular alignment of the assemblies. Upon confirmation, an actuator advances the movable contacts to establish electrical connection for charging. During decoupling, the contacts are retracted before the coupling assembly is withdrawn. The arrangement prevents premature contact, reduces arcing and contact damage, and enables reliable automated charging despite vehicle-positioning variation.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
